summary: Provisioning hang: device stuck 'Applying Policies' after depot eSIM activation changes MDM routing
description: Issue summary: Multiple Lenovo X13s units returned from depot repair are hanging at Intune Autopilot status 'Applying Policies' during first-boot provisioning. Impact: New hires and returned assets cannot complete provisioning; machines remain unusable until manual intervention. Environment: Production autopilot profile, depot image (Win11 23H2), corporate network with DHCP/DNS on provisioning VLAN; affected devices have embedded LTE modems with eSIM profiles reactivated by depot vendor. Observed behavior: Devices boot, start Autopilot, reach 'Applying Policies' step and then stall for >30 minutes. Intune console reports MDM registration but SCEP/cert enrollment fails with timeouts when device is on cellular route. Expected behavior: Autopilot completes policy application over corporate wired or SSID network and device enrolls successfully. Attachments: device serials list, dump of Autopilot state, APNs logs from depot vendor.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Depot performs NVMe replacement and firmware reflash on X13s and re-enables eSIM profile via vendor Mobile Operator portal.
2) Device shipped back to end user and powered on in provisioning VLAN with USB dock attached.
3) Device initializes Autopilot, downloads policies, then attempts certificate enrollment (SCEP) and MDM registration.
4) Enrollment hangs; device reports successful AzureAD join but SCEP fails with timeout; UI stays at 'Applying Policies'.
logs: Intune SCEP error: 0x8018002a (timeout waiting for CA response)
MDM enrollment: device reported as 'Managed' but SCEP status=Pending; MDMDeviceId mismatch between Autopilot record and device-reported ID
Network trace (tcpdump): device attempting outbound to corp-ocsp/redwood-ca over 443 but traffic egresses via cellular APN and hits carrier DNS proxy
APNs (depot vendor): eSIM activation timestamps match repair completion times; ICCID changed on 3 serials
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: eSIM activation causes routing preference to cellular during early OOBE, sending SCEP traffic over carrier network where corporate CA endpoints are unreachable or intercepted.
Hypothesis 2: Depot vendor re-provisioned eSIM with a different ICCID leading to mismatch in our device registration flow and Intune treating device as re-enrolled (MDMDeviceId change).

Finding: Packet captures show DNS resolution for corp CA endpoints resolved to carrier proxy IPs when WWAN interface is up; on devices where WWAN was physically disabled in firmware, provisioning succeeded.
Finding: Intune logs show CA responded but our firewall blocks connections arriving from unexpected public IP ranges; when traffic egresses over carrier APN the CA return path is dropped by rule set.
Temporary evidence: reproducer tested by enabling airplane mode after Autopilot begins — device falls back to wired Wi-Fi and SCEP completes successfully.
comments: Leah Kim (Reporter) 2026-02-28: Noticed 4/10 returned units from depot stuck. Raised after onboarding desk reported two users unable to complete first-day setup.
Depot Vendor (Field Ops) 2026-03-01: Confirmed eSIM reactivation per policy; provided activation logs and ICCIDs.
SRE - Maya Chen 2026-03-02: Captures show SCEP traffic leaving on ppp0 (WWAN). Blocking carrier egress during provisioning fixed case in lab.

Ravi Desai (Assignee) 2026-03-03: Planned change: update depot checklist to suspend eSIM and reflash modem with disabled profile before shipping. Also will add Intune policy to prefer Ethernet/SSID for SCEP during Autopilot.
Security - Omar Khalid 2026-03-04: Raised concern about CA endpoints reachable from public IPs. Will temp add allowlist for carrier APNs used by depot while we implement longer-term fix.
Ravi Desai 2026-03-06: Implemented depot checklist change; two test units confirmed provisioning without manual intervention. Scheduling rollout and runbook updates.
resolution: Workaround deployed: depot vendors instructed to disable/reactivate eSIM after OOBE completes; depot checklist updated to put modem into 'airplane' state before shipping.
Configuration change: Intune Autopilot profile updated to require network interface priority (Ethernet/Wi‑Fi) for SCEP enrollment during initial provisioning.
Firewall/Networking: Temporary allowlist added for specific carrier APN IP ranges used by depot to allow CA callbacks while rollouts proceed.

Follow-ups: Create automated check in device QA to verify WWAN interface state prior to shipping; create monitoring alert for Autopilot 'Applying Policies' >15 minutes for depot-returned serials; security to review allowlist expiry.
Status: Partial fix in place and testing passed on 5 repro units; next step is org-wide depot rollout and deprecation of temporary allowlist.
